themes_detail.label: Food Poisoning Spike
themes_detail.summary: Food poisoning complaints in CD212 surged to 4 reports THIS WEEK compared to a baseline average of 0.5 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 700% spike (z-score: 7.0)—suggesting a potential foodborne illness outbreak or cluster affecting residents.
evidence: 4 food poisoning complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly baseline over prior 8 weeks
700% increase with z-score of 7.0 (statistically significant anomaly)
Aligns with concurrent spike in food establishment complaints (10 reports 3 weeks ago)
reporting_angles: Investigate whether complaints are clustered around specific food vendors, restaurants, or food service locations
Contact NYC Department of Health to determine if they've identified linked cases or are conducting inspections in the district

themes_detail.label: Overgrown Tree/Branches Surge
themes_detail.summary: Tree and branch complaints escalated sharply THIS WEEK to 13 reports versus a 8-week average of 4.4 weekly—a 197% spike (z-score: 4.62)—indicating potential public safety hazards from unmaintained vegetation.
evidence: 13 overgrown tree/branch complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 4.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Aligns with standing community board budget request for new Parks Department maintenance equipment
reporting_angles: Map complaint locations to identify geographic clusters and determine if specific neighborhoods lack maintenance
Interview Parks Department about maintenance capacity and whether this spike reflects seasonal demand or deferred upkeep

themes_detail.label: Panhandling and Homelessness Uptick
themes_detail.summary: Panhandling complaints reached 3 reports THIS WEEK (500% above the 0.5 weekly baseline), while homeless person assistance complaints peaked at 9 reports 3 WEEKS AGO (454% spike)—signaling a potential concentration of unhoused individuals or inadequate outreach services.
evidence: 3 panhandling complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly baseline (500% spike, z-score: 3.54)
9 homeless person assistance complaints 3 WEEKS AGO vs. 1.6 weekly baseline (454% spike, z-score: 4.1)
No local social service agencies or shelters mentioned in available data—potential service gap
reporting_angles: Interview local homeless outreach organizations and NYC Department of Social Services to understand service availability and whether demand has increased
Document resident concerns about panhandling hotspots and whether they cluster in commercial or transit areas

themes_detail.label: Vehicle Noise and Scooter Complaints
themes_detail.summary: Vehicle noise complaints peaked 2 WEEKS AGO at 27 reports (196% above the 9.1 weekly average, z-score: 4.01), while e-scooter complaints hit 3 reports LAST WEEK (500% spike)—indicating rising disruptions from unregulated street use and motorized vehicles.
evidence: 27 vehicle noise complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 9.1 weekly average (196% increase, z-score: 4.01)
3 e-scooter complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly baseline (500% spike, z-score: 3.54)
Illegal parking also elevated at 264 complaints LAST WEEK vs. 209.9 average (26% increase)
reporting_angles: Survey residents to identify where vehicle noise and scooter use is most disruptive (specific streets, times of day)
Contact NYPD and Department of Transportation about enforcement capacity for illegal scooter use and vehicle noise ordinances

themes_detail.label: Illegal Parking Pressure
themes_detail.summary: Illegal parking complaints rose to 264 reports LAST WEEK from a 209.9 weekly average—a 26% increase (z-score: 3.99)—compounding existing strain on parking availability and street access in the district.
evidence: 264 illegal parking complaints LAST WEEK vs. 209.9 weekly baseline (26% increase, z-score: 3.99)
Illegal parking is the third-highest complaint category over 90 days (2834 total complaints)
Blocked driveway complaints also consistently elevated (1636 over 90 days), suggesting systemic parking pressure
reporting_angles: Analyze whether spike correlates with specific events, construction, or changes in parking policy
Interview residents about enforcement visibility and whether increased complaints reflect worsening conditions or improved reporting
